Bulgarian

[edit]
Bulgarian Wikipedia has an article on:
река
Wikipedia bg

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Old Church Slavonic рещи (rešti), from Proto-Slavic *reťi.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [rɛˈkɤ]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -kɤ
  • Syllabification(key): ре‧ка

Verb

[edit]

река́ • (reká) first-singular present indicative, pf

  1. to say, to tell, to speak, to utter
    Synonyms: изду́мам (izdúmam), изрека́ (izreká), ка́жа (káža)
    Слу́шай какво́ ще ти река́: ви́ждаш ли два́та бря́ста?
    Slúšaj kakvó šte ti reká: víždaš li dváta brjásta?
    Listen to what I will tell you: do you see the two elms?
  2. (colloquial) to order, to command
    Synonyms: заръ́чам (zarǎ́čam), заповя́дам (zapovjádam), поръ́чам (porǎ́čam)
    Щом ти рече́ш, ня́ма да хо́дя на учи́лище.
    Štom ti rečéš, njáma da hódja na učílište.
    Since you order it, I won't go to school.
  3. (colloquial) to ask
    Synonyms: запи́там (zapítam), попи́там (popítam)
  4. (colloquial) to answer, to reply
    Synonym: отгово́ря (otgovórja)
    Каже́те ми, рече́те, / туй любовта́ какво́ е?
    Kažéte mi, rečéte, / tuj ljubovtá kakvó e?
    Tell me, answer, / what is this love?
  5. (colloquial, with да (da)) to decide, to intend (to do something)
    Synonyms: нака́ня се (nakánja se), на́мисля (námislja), реша́ (rešá)
    Вечерта́ ня́кои жени́ ре́кли да оти́дат да запа́лят свещ.
    Večertá njákoi žení rékli da otídat da zapáljat svešt.
    In the evening, some women decided to go and light a candle.
  6. to mean, to signify
    Synonyms: зна́ча (znáča), означа́ (označá)
    Какво́ ще рече́ туй не́що?
    Kakvó šte rečé tuj néšto?
    What does this thing mean?
  7. (reflexive with си) to say to oneself, to think
    Synonym: поми́сля си (pomíslja si)
    Сега́ е ло́шо, ре́кох си и ми́слех да бя́гам ли, и́ли да се кри́я в гора́та.
    Segá e lóšo, rékoh si i mísleh da bjágam li, íli da se kríja v goráta.
    Now it's bad, I thought to myself and was wondering whether to run away or hide in the forest.

Etymology 2

[edit]

Inherited from Old Church Slavonic рѣка (rěka), from Proto-Slavic *rěka.

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • ря́ка (rjáka) — Moesian dialects

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [rɛˈka]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ka
  • Homophone: Река (Reka)
  • Syllabification(key): ре‧ка

Noun

[edit]

река́ • (reká) f (relational adjective ре́чен, diminutive реки́ца or реки́чка)

  1. river (a large and often winding stream which drains a land mass, carrying water down from higher areas to a lower point, oftentimes ending in another body of water, such as an ocean or in an inland sea)
  2. (figuratively) river (a large number or multitude of people, animals, vehicles, objects, etc., moving in one direction)

[edit]
Russian Wikipedia has an article on:
река
Wikipedia ru

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • рѣка́ (rěká) — pre-1918 spelling

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old East Slavic рѣка (rěka), from Proto-Slavic *rěka, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃royHkeh₂, from *h₃reyH-, whence English runlet and rivulet and Spanish río.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [rʲɪˈka]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

река́ • (reká) f inan (genitive реки́, nominative plural ре́ки, genitive plural рек, relational adjective речно́й, diminutive ре́чка or речу́шка)

  1. river, stream
    Coordinate term: бе́рег m (béreg)
    Meronym: ру́сло n (rúslo)

Serbo-Croatian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • рије́ка (Ijekavian)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *rěka, from Proto-Indo-European *(H)rey- (“to flow”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /rěːka/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Hyphenation: ре‧ка

Noun

[edit]

ре́ка f (Latin spelling réka)

  1. river
    Крањска, Корушка и Штајерска леже у сливу река Саве, Драве, односно Муре. ― Carniola, Carinthia and Styria are located in the drainage basin of the rivers Sava, Drava and Mura, respectively.
